Management 
 
* ABCD approach to resuscitation 
 
* Hypovolaemia 
20 ml/kg Balsol/Ringers Lactate bolus 
 
* Septic shock  
 
Fluids:  
20 ml/kg Balsol/Ringers Lactate bolus 
Antibiotics: 
AugmentinÒ 30mg/kg IV 
Urgent Surgical consult 
 
* Analgesia 
 
Morphine 0.1mg/kg 
 
* Antiemetic 
 
MaxolonÒ 0.1mg/kg (not in children < 1 years old) 
 
* Investigations 
 
U-dipstix on all patients 
 
U-bHCG on all female patients 
 
Laboratory:  
FBC/CRP/U&E  
 
Radiological: 
Graded compression ultrasound 
 
 
 
CXR erect if perforation is suspected 
Tailor other investigations to clinical findings & to rule in/rule out other differential 
diagnoses 
 
*  Disposition 
 
Urgent Surgical consultation 
Patients in the 
low risk group   
do not have a 
zero risk.  
Treat according 
to your clinical 
judgment. 
Special Population Groups 
 
* Paediatric: may present with more non-specific or atypical symptoms. 
* Pregnancy: due to displacement of the uterus, presentation may be atypical.                       
                         A leukocytosis in pregnancy is normal. 
* Elderly: do not mount the usual inflammatory response. The usual signs & symptoms  
                  of appendicitis may be reduced, atypical or even absent. Tend to present later. 
* Immunocompromised: do not mount the usual inflammatory response. 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
